speaker: M. M. Kapranov
title: Baker functions, spinors, and twistor transforms
summary: The talk joins the construction of line bundles from exponential principal parts to twistor descriptions of Yang--Mills equations. The manuscript distinguishes the newly generalized Baker-function construction from material inspired by Witten, Clifford algebra, and the four-dimensional Penrose--Ward correspondence. A. Goncharov supplies the spinor explanation. The ten-dimensional projective diagram is too compressed to support an additional theorem. Earlier related exposition occurs at 1975-374.4, 1975-379.7, 1977-432.15, 1978-455.6, and 1982-592.7; these are connections, not evidence for a recurring open problem.

speaker: V. I. Arnold
title: Zeros of Abelian integrals and Petrov nonoscillation
summary: Arnold asks for bounds on zeros of Abelian integrals and reports Petrov's sharp cubic-Hamiltonian theorem. The page then moves through Chebyshev spaces, Picard--Fuchs equations, vanishing periods, and two Jacobian-algebra examples. The compactness and degree qualifications are essential. A general linear-independence sentence is false literally; it is not used to justify Petrov's theorem.

speaker: A. V. Zelevinsky
title: Jacobi triple product through binary words and partitions
summary: The correct expanded triple product is followed by an incorrect compressed Pochhammer version. Zelevinsky then gives a combinatorial proof through partitions, eventually constant binary words, a distinguished gap, and two sets of odd distances. The method is attributed in the notebook to Leibenzon; Arnold adds the Young-diagram interpretation. The proof is elementary exposition, not an unsolved partition identity. Related encodings occur at 1976-415.1 and 1981-548.1--2.

speaker: A. V. Zelevinsky, with A. A. Beilinson
title: Reports on Vigneras, triple products, and trace Paley--Wiener
summary: The 16 September heading starts below the completed partition argument on P001203. It reports Vigneras's work and the Piatetski-Shapiro--Rallis triple product, then sketches the trace transform and unramified families. The separate Beilinson heading in the middle of P001204 belongs to this same meeting and concerns the quadratic Hermitian space and theta correspondence; it is not the 23 September Beilinson talk. Vigneras's intervening explanation at the top of P001204 has its own record 646.

speaker: M.-F. Vigneras
title: Bernstein support and the trace Paley--Wiener theorem
summary: Vigneras's short intervention continues the preceding trace-transform discussion. The two essential corrections are that the Bernstein variety parametrizes cuspidal support rather than individual irreducibles, and that the trace Paley--Wiener theorem requires a uniform compact-open invariance bound, in addition to algebraicity along induced families. The item is placed before record 645 because that is their order on the page.

speaker: B. L. Feigin
title: Worldsheets, area actions, and Polyakov integration
summary: Feigin describes string worldsheets and the passage from the induced-area functional to integration over a map and an independent metric. The formulas are the established Nambu--Goto and Polyakov constructions. Statements about all particles, a crystal-growth analogy, and an asserted operator/integral correspondence lack enough detail for theorem identification. The fixed-metric Gaussian step is precise; the full measure over surfaces is left formal. The continuation on 23 September begins only after Beilinson's conclusion on P001207.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: A central diagonal section of the four-dimensional cube
summary: Gelfand poses one elementary geometry problem, explicitly addressed to a ninth-grade audience. The answer is a regular octahedron; a complete coordinate verification is supplied as an annotation. The question is not an unresolved research problem.

speaker: A. A. Beilinson, with I. M. Gelfand interventions
title: Adeles, automorphic representations, Satake parameters, and L-functions
summary: Beilinson introduces the automorphic setting for the announced work of Piatetski-Shapiro and Rallis. Gelfand explains p-adic expansions and points to Connes's Bourbaki lecture. The mathematical core passes from adeles and congruence quotients to restricted tensor products, spherical representations, dual groups, and Euler factors. Several handwritten shortcuts are false literally: the unrestricted product of completions, the punctured-sphere descriptions, and the suggestion that local representation lists alone determine the automorphic spectrum. The general occurrence problem is separated from the already established formalism.

speaker: B. L. Feigin
title: Strings: area, energy, and independent metrics
summary: The continuation begins halfway down P001207, after the preceding discussion of automorphic \(L\)-functions. Feigin passes from the area of an immersed surface to the Polyakov action on a map and an independent metric, then to the formal quotient by reparametrizations. Several shortcuts conflate the area Hessian with the fixed-metric energy Hessian and harmonicity with conformality. Gelfand's intervention about minimal surfaces is retained without silently identifying the uncertain historical attribution.

speaker: B. L. Feigin
title: Spectral determinants, the conformal anomaly, and dimension 26
summary: The recorder explicitly arrived half an hour late. The surviving notes concern zeta determinants of Dolbeault Laplacians on tensor powers of the tangent bundle, heat regularization, the polynomial \(6j^2+6j+1\), and cancellation of the bosonic string anomaly at target dimension \(26\). The argument is expository: Polyakov's paper appeared in 1981. Real versus complex determinant conventions, zero modes, curvature normalization, and the distinction between a classical Liouville equation and a quantum integral require separate corrections.

speaker: D. B. Fuchs
title: Recapitulation of Feigin: gauge fixing the surface metric
summary: Fuchs repeats Feigin's account on a closed oriented surface of genus at least two: a formal Gaussian integration over maps, a conformal slice, and the Faddeev--Popov Jacobian. A question about a surface analogue of Wiener measure and Gelfand's physical interpretation of the extra string scale are distinct interventions. The omitted Teichmüller directions and the final identification of the ghost operator with the ordinary Hodge Laplacian are substantive mathematical gaps, rather than new open questions.

speaker: Yu. S. Ryzhikova
title: Recognizing identities in lattices of subspaces
summary: Ryzhikova announces an algorithm for identities in lattices of finite-dimensional linear subspaces, based on a computable dimension bound followed by a decision procedure in fixed dimension. This is identifiable with her 1987 Doklady paper. The manuscript heading is \(21/X/85\), whereas the catalogue gives 21 September; the present date follows the manuscript. This contribution precedes Fuchs's record 652 on the same page.

speaker: D. B. Fuchs; B. L. Feigin (intervention)
title: Fixed conformal structure, moduli, and the Liouville action
summary: After Fuchs's short recap, the notebook explicitly marks Feigin's intervention. Fixing a point of moduli separates the conformal factor from the remaining \(3g-3\) complex parameters. The anomaly calculation and critical dimension recur, and the determinant variation is integrated into a Liouville action. The asserted equivalence of solving its classical equation and evaluating its functional integral is not valid as stated. The date is corrected from the catalogue's September to the manuscript's October.

speaker: Werner Müller
title: Characteristic numbers, conic operators, and Hilbert modular cusps
summary: Müller first reports Cheeger--Gromov's characteristic-number results for complete finite-volume manifolds with bounded curvature and a compact topological core. He then discusses conical heat expansions, eta corrections to the signature, an index question for more general regular singular operators, and locally symmetric examples. The last example matches his published 1984 work on Hilbert modular cusp defects, though its exact handwritten constant has not been checked in that inaccessible full text. The displayed cone metric has the wrong exponent in the manuscript itself.

speaker: B. L. Feigin
title: Determinant lines and anomaly cancellation
summary: Feigin recasts the previous determinant calculation in the determinant of Dolbeault cohomology. Harmonic representatives give a Hodge metric, and the zeta determinant supplies the Quillen correction. Tensor products whose anomaly coefficients sum to zero carry a metric independent of the chosen conformal representative. The notebook uses the dual of Quillen's own determinant-line convention, explaining why its squared norm is divided, rather than multiplied, by the spectral determinant.

speaker: Yu. S. Ryzhikova
title: Perfect elements and cubicles in free modular lattices
summary: The heading expressly identifies this as an exposition of Gelfand and Ponomarev's work. It defines perfect elements through compatible complements and indecomposable representations, sketches the recursive upper and lower Boolean cubicles, and ends with complete irreducibility in characteristic zero. The exact source is the 1974 Russian Mathematical Surveys paper, with earlier seminar occurrences in 1973. Several indices and the cubicle cardinality need emendation; no completeness conjecture absent from these pages is imported from the source.

speaker: B. L. Feigin
title: Virasoro modules, Sugawara and coset constructions, and screening integrals
summary: Feigin links strings to Virasoro representation theory and hypergeometric functions. The notes state the Verma-module reducibility criterion, construct Virasoro actions from affine currents, take the coset difference, and introduce Selberg and Dotsenko--Fateev integrals. These are identifiable established constructions. Important faithful errors include the Kac-polynomial coefficient, incompatible central-charge signs, a missing noncritical-level hypothesis, and incomplete screening-cycle and integral conventions.

speaker: A. M. Vershik
title: Configuration spaces, polytope universality and lattices
summary: The talk moves from Grassmannian configuration strata and isotopy of classes defined by determinant signs to realization spaces of polytopes. Mn\"ev universality was already circulating and published; the statement about simplicial four-polytopes retains an informal hedge and is not established by either general four-dimensional universality or variable-dimensional neighborly universality. The final part concerns geometric lattices, the Fano obstruction, lattice representations and the Pudl\'ak--T\r{u}ma theorem. Gelfand adds a historical intervention. The manuscript begins on P001229 and ends on the upper part of P001231; the supplied catalogue range overlaps adjacent talks.

speaker: B. L. Feigin
title: Dual amplitudes, free bosons and vertex operators
summary: The first string lecture introduces elastic-scattering invariants and the Veneziano amplitude, then reconstructs amplitudes through oscillator Fock spaces, Virasoro modes, normal-ordered exponential vertices and contraction identities. The notebook asserts uniqueness under conditions that do not even fix an overall normalization. Its five-point evaluation remark lacks the exponents and a specified meaning of evaluation, so no open problem is manufactured. These are mainly established constructions; zero modes, metric signs and plane versus cylinder conventions account for several essential corrections. The Feigin heading occurs midway down P001231.

speaker: B. L. Feigin
title: Physical quotients, the no-ghost theorem and lattice vertices
summary: Feigin defines the constrained physical space and spurious quotient, states the critical no-ghost result, and connects screening residues with Kac--Moody algebras and transverse DDF oscillators. Gelfand identifies the Monster/string connection. The strongest needed qualifications are the nonzero-momentum exception, the quotient by null states, the distinction between ghosts and tachyons, and the momentum normalization in DDF brackets. The last part on P001238 ends immediately before Zelevinsky begins; it does not include that page in its entirety.

speaker: A. V. Zelevinsky
title: Schubert cells, divided differences and Schubert polynomials
summary: This is explicitly an exposition of Lascoux--Sch\"utzenberger, following the 1973 Bernstein--Gelfand--Gelfand paper. It compares the Borel presentation with the Schubert basis and constructs polynomial representatives by divided differences. The missing top-class factor \(1/n!\) and the divided-difference sign are genuine mathematical inconsistencies in the manuscript. Earlier related occurrences include 1971-239.1--2 (Schubert homology), 1979-483.1 (reduced words), 1979-484.3 (Schubert closures), and 1982-575.1 (Grassmannian cohomology); no earlier problem identifier matches a new open question here.

speaker: B. L. Feigin
title: Normal ordering, even lattices and affine current representations
summary: The continuation revisits Virasoro and no-ghost, then constructs root Lie algebras and affine current representations from even lattices and sign cocycles, concluding with the DDF recipe. Gelfand asks how normal ordering depends on the underlying geometry. Krichever--Novikov supplies a nearby later construction, but the intervention does not specify a unique theorem. The module assertion depending only on momentum norm fails at zero versus nonzero null momentum; the sign cocycle itself forces the evenness temporarily waived in the notes. The Leech-lattice aside must be kept distinct from the norm-two-root construction because that lattice is rootless. The next dated talk starts on P001245 and is outside this record.

speaker: S. P. Novikov
title: Two-dimensional Schrödinger operators at one energy
summary: The talk moves from the failure of a naive all-energy analogy with one-dimensional inverse scattering to Manakov triples and the two-point Baker--Akhiezer construction. It explains potential and reality reductions by involutions of the spectral curve, Prym theta functions, and the two-dimensional analogue of KdV. The main constructions were published in 1976 and 1984. Several derivatives in the notebook are internally inconsistent; these are mathematical emendations of faithfully transcribed formulas. The final rapidly decaying assertion is less precise than the periodic construction. The actual heading is on P001245; P001244 still belongs to Feigin.

speaker: V. G. Knizhnik
title: Strings, moduli and quadratic differentials
summary: The second talk of 16 December constructs the critical bosonic-string measure in conformal gauge, explains the role of quadratic and Beltrami differentials, and works through the torus determinant before sketching higher-genus theta formulas. Novikov intervenes about the Schottky problem. The notes combine classical geometry, Polyakov\textquotesingle s 1981 formalism, and material soon published by Belavin and Knizhnik. They do not provide a rigorous measure on all embedded surfaces. The heading says \ru{Д. Книжник. (Дима)}; the catalogue identification as V.~G.~Knizhnik is retained with the discrepancy explicit.

title: The catalogue heading: Year 1986
summary: This is the catalogue heading \ru{Год 1986}, not a separate mathematical talk. The next supplied leaf begins Beilinson\textquotesingle s dated talk on 17 February 1986. No independent mathematical item is assigned to the heading, and its page reference denotes the boundary only. The academic-year item prefix remains 1985.

speaker: A. A. Beilinson
title: Quillen determinants, anomaly cancellation and the Mumford form
summary: Beilinson recasts the string determinant in the language of determinant lines and their Quillen metrics. A finite-dimensional comparison exposes a dual-line inconsistency in the written norm formula. The anomaly polynomial leads to the combination \(\lambda_2\lambda_1^{-13}\); Belavin intervenes with the holomorphic measure, low-genus theta formulas and divergences. The final uniqueness argument needs an overall normalization. P001258 and P001259 begin separately headed Kontsevich and Morozov talks (catalogue records 667 and 668), and are treated as adjacent evidence in a separate supplement, not assigned to Beilinson or counted as additional records in this chapter.
